clue.text: Weapons carried personally by team members

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: Players on a squad each carry a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidearms are pistols or swords worn at the belt by an individual soldier.

clue.text: Fights a dupe's receiving credit

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the dupe holds the credit inside

parts.note: a sap is a dupe, and a dupe's is a sap's

explanation.surface: Fights break out when a gullible person gets credit.
explanation.walkthrough: A sap is a gullible person; 'receiving' is the container signal, 'a dupe's' holding the credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps are brawls or minor fights, in informal use.

clue.text: Twice as loud, by mistake

indicators.note: by mistake suggests letters set down in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Something came out twice as loud by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubly means in two ways or to twice the degree.

clue.text: A fellow advocate

parts.note: a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A man who argues a case.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts for or speaks on behalf of another, like an advocate.

clue.text: Fickle possibly but meal is taken

indicators.note: taken in the sense of taken apart, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Maybe moody, but the lunch has been eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' rearranges BUT and MEAL; 'possibly' says fickle is one example of the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutable means liable to change, as a fickle person is.

clue.text: The man in charge, or general manager

indicators.note: in says the name sits inside the run of words charge, or general

explanation.surface: Someone asks who is boss: the man in charge or the general manager.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a choice of bosses, but 'in' points into the words 'charge, or general', and 'manager' just completes the picture of a man running things.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name stands for any man, as in 'by George'.

clue.text: A complaint as regards public transport

parts.note: to eye someone is to regard them, so regards gives eyes
a train is public transport

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about buses and trains.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is a minor ailment of tired, aching eyes.

clue.text: Gave up and faced the wall

explanation.surface: Someone surrendered and turned to face a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: To render a wall is to coat it with plaster or cement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendered means handed over or surrendered, and also coated a wall with a plaster facing.

clue.text: Judge set a mite wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests letters placed incorrectly and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A court official gets a small sum wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge an amount roughly.

clue.text: Concerned with restricting new outlet for game

indicators.note: one piece hems in the other, so it holds the shuffled letters inside it

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: new signals the letters of outlet made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone worried about controlling a new shop outlet for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal on 'outlet', and 'restricting' makes the word for concerned with hold those letters; outlet looks like a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game played on a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Greek character into vegetable matter as food of a sort

indicators.note: into says the Greek letter goes inside the vegetable matter

parts.note: peat is decayed vegetable matter dug from bogs
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man gets into compost, eating something odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is the container signal; 'vegetable matter' sounds like greens, but it is the bog fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is an edible nut, a kind of snack food.

clue.text: The man backing British Rail must be simple!

parts.note: he is the man

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the railway letters are read backwards

parts.note: BR stood for British Rail, the old UK railway

explanation.surface: A man supporting the national railway must be naive.
explanation.walkthrough: A simple, as a noun, is a medicinal plant; 'simple!' looks like an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage a simple is a medicinal plant, a herbal remedy.

clue.text: Providing a friend with furniture that's tasteful

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Giving a friend some furniture shows good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Here tasteful means pleasant to eat, agreeable on the palate.

clue.text: An article by servicemen generating some heat

parts.note: the is the definite article
RM is the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about soldiers that causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat energy, used in measuring gas supply.

clue.text: Singing for pleasure?

explanation.surface: A question whether people sing because they enjoy it.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee is an unaccompanied part-song for voices, and glee is also delight or joy.

clue.text: It's most foolish however-especially in America

explanation.surface: Someone calls a choice the silliest, at least in American eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, least wise means the opposite of wisest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being least sensible is being most foolish, and leastwise is an American word for anyway or at any rate.

clue.text: The most daring underclothing

parts.note: a bra is a woman's undergarment
a vest is an undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: A remark that the boldest outfit is just underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: One word supplies two garments, BRA and VEST; a vest in Britain is a sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravest is the superlative of brave, meaning most courageous.

clue.text: Exceptional individual

explanation.surface: A remarkable person.
explanation.definitionFit: Singular means remarkable or unusual, and also single, one of a kind.

clue.text: Soldiers allowed to take possession of a vehicle when appropriate

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: taking possession means holding, so the permission word holds the vehicle

parts.note: let means allowed
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Troops are permitted to commandeer a van where suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take possession of' is the container signal; RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevant means pertinent or fitting to the matter at hand.

clue.text: Repeat of a trite broadcast by egghead

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of egg is E

explanation.surface: An intellectual delivers a repeat of a banal programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' makes ITERAT from A TRITE; 'egghead' is read as egg's head, its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do again, a synonym for repeat.

clue.text: To be retrospective is not good

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the word for to be is read in reverse

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: Dwelling on the past is a bad thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil is wickedness, the opposite of good.

clue.text: Figure it's about one

parts.note: c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Working out a sum where the answer is roughly one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone is a solid geometric figure tapering to a point.

clue.text: A letter from the metropolis?

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a letter posted in the big city.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital is an upper-case letter, and a capital is the chief city of a country.

clue.text: The pictures came in damaged

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Film reels arrived in poor condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures is going to the movies.

clue.text: Flag but go on writing about a certain point

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the writing phrase goes round the point

parts.note: to pen on is to continue writing
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone tires but keeps writing about a particular issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside PEN ON; 'Flag' looks like a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow pointed banner.

clue.text: How Scots cry hail

explanation.surface: A note on how people in Scotland call out a welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect to greet is to weep, and to greet someone is to salute or hail them.

clue.text: In a deadlock four will be unaffected

indicators.note: In at the front says the number goes inside the deadlock

parts.note: an impasse is a deadlock
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people stuck in a stalemate stay calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the start is the container signal: the Roman four goes inside the word for a deadlock.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassive means showing no emotion, unmoved by events.

clue.text: Warning: she's a seductive creature

explanation.surface: A caution about an alluring woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a loud alarm, and in myth a sea nymph who lured sailors.

clue.text: The Parisian, a big noise, makes the introduction

parts.note: le is French for the
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A loud French celebrity opens the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big noise' looks like a celebrity, but it is just DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead-in is an opening passage or remark that introduces what follows.

clue.text: A way to encourage a swimmer

parts.note: St is street, a way
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: Advice on how to cheer a swimmer along.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturgeon is a large fish, valued for its roe as caviar.

clue.text: The cad's upsetting retort

indicators.note: upsetting means overturning, so the letters of retort fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A scoundrel's hurtful comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotter is an old-fashioned word for a scoundrel, someone who behaves badly.

clue.text: A green banana left a worker in anguish

indicators.note: in says the first pieces sit inside the word for anguish

parts.note: pain is anguish
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A labourer stuck with an unripe banana is in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; a plantain is the banana cooked green in the Caribbean and West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a starchy cooking banana, eaten while green.
